summary: Validated backend fix for PUT /api/shows/titles/{title_id} duplicate-name guard. All 4 pytest scenarios pass: (1) same-name update with only presenter changes succeeds (200), (2) renaming to another title's exact name returns 400 'already exists', (3) unique rename succeeds and is persisted via GET, (4) case-insensitive duplicate rename still rejected with 400. Original record state restored after each mutating test.
action_items: Note: Review request referenced path '/api/show-titles/{id}' but the actual mounted route is '/api/shows/titles/{id}' (shows_router prefix '/shows'). Test uses the correct path. If a frontend is still calling '/api/show-titles' it will 404 — please confirm the frontend calls '/api/shows/titles'.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix in routers/shows.py (lines 235-252) correctly short-circuits the duplicate check with name_changed guard before running the Mongo regex query, and re.escape(new_name) prevents regex-metachar crashes. Logic looks correct and matches intent.

Minor: update_dict is built via {k:v for k,v in model_dump().items() if v is not None} — this means callers cannot clear optional fields by sending null. default_presenter_ids is handled separately below (ok), but other nullable fields may be impossible to blank. Not in scope for this bug.
seed_data_creation: None. Tests pick the first two existing show titles, mutate, and restore original name/presenters.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend route for show titles is /api/shows/titles (not /api/show-titles). Admin login returns access_token. X-Main-Site slug 'radiogroep' is required for main-site scoped operations. Pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_show_title_update.py can be re-run as a regression test.
rca of the issue: Original bug: duplicate-name check ran unconditionally on PUT, matching 'A show title with this name already exists' even on self when fields other than name were edited. Although the Mongo filter had {'id': {'$ne': title_id}}, the symptom reported by the user still fired — likely because the frontend or server-side normalization produced a different id comparison in some code path, or the regex collided due to unescaped metacharacters. Fix: compare normalized old vs new name first (name_changed guard) and skip the duplicate query entirely when the name is unchanged; also escape regex metachars in new_name. Verified: scenario 1 now returns 200 with the modified default_presenter_ids echoed back; scenarios 2 & 4 still reject renames that collide with other titles (case-insensitive); scenario 3 confirms legitimate rename works and persists.
